about: Maison M. Chapoutier has made wine in Tain-l’Hermitage, in the northern Rhône, since 1808. Under Michel Chapoutier, who took over in the early 1990s, the house became one of France’s pioneers of biodynamic farming, practiced since 1991, and is known for its single-vineyard, terroir-driven wines. Its family motto is “Fac et spera,” do and hope. Les Bécasses, French for “the woodcocks,” is its Côte-Rôtie, from the steep, terraced slopes above the Rhône at the northern tip of the region.

The wine is 100% Syrah, blended from well-exposed parcels across the appellation: La Brocarde, La Viallière, Côte Rozier, Côte Blonde, Côte Brune and Les Coteaux de Tupin. The soils are mica-schist rich in iron, with loess in the hollows. The grapes are hand-harvested, destemmed and fermented in concrete with native yeasts and daily punch-downs for three to four weeks. The wine then ages 14 to 16 months, about 80% in mostly new oak barrels and 20% in stainless steel.
The house describes raspberry and violet over a base of spice and undergrowth, with a touch of black olive, then a full, velvety palate with notes of wood and a spicy, vanilla finish.
